correctness.rationale: Unit variance, two distinct points, strictly positive weights and all quantifiers are explicit. The unique singleton is the weighted mean; its global dual condition is exactly the sharp Kearns--Saul inequality (Schlemm 2014, Theorem 1.1, checked in full primary text). An explicitly differentiated two-normal critical-point equation bounds all optimizer supports by two. Strict concavity in the two fitted values and independence of Gaussian kernel evaluation vectors ensure uniqueness, including the critical dual second contact. The two nondegenerate critical maxima and compactness yield the distinct support-location transition; Beta-Gamma normalization and monotone atanh(x)/x yield the exact random-weight probability. A standalone checker was executed and passed 29849 finite diagnostics; the continuum proof is analytical, not inferred from grids.

The closest general literature supplies key tools but no stronger published statement covering all conclusions was identified.

value.rationale: The exact count of mixture components under randomly weighted likelihood is a natural finite-sample specialization of Jiang 2026. The phase boundary is sharp for all positive weights, not an arbitrary finite numerical example. It separates the global dual feasibility and local-curvature thresholds, identifies a separated low-mass emerging component, and gives a closed probability law under the actual Gamma reweighting mechanism motivating the question. These facts guide support interpretation and expose finite-sample instability; no broader-rate improvement is asserted.
